document.headline: Work Queue 2.0 became fast, guided, and ready for real operational use.

subject.mainFocus: Connecting task templates across the full application stack and proving the upgraded task-creation workflow through layered validation, deployment, and desktop/mobile testing.
subject.description: Klinswork Work Queue 2.0 Phase 2 update for July 25, 2026, covering task templates, formal validation, startup-data integration, interface testing, deployment, and mobile verification.

narrative.promptingSituation: Work Queue 2.0 had a populated Task_Templates sheet, but the data was not yet connected through the backend, validation, startup response, form, browser behavior, and deployed user workflow.
narrative.initialUnderstanding: The next useful improvement was to replace free-text task creation with a guided template-assisted flow without removing user flexibility.
narrative.intendedOutcome: Create a fast, reliable task-creation process that worked across the entire stack and was proven on desktop and mobile.
narrative.approach: Build and verify one layer at a time: service, retrieval test, schema validation, startup data, rendered form, browser behavior, integration test, deployment, realistic desktop test, and mobile test.

progression.title: Template service
progression.description: Created TemplateService.gs and normalized active template records.
progression.result: 10 active templates and 6 categories were retrievable and correctly sorted.

progression.title: Validation and startup integration
progression.result: The system returned templates and categories with zero validation errors or warnings.

progression.title: Guided New Task workflow
progression.description: Rebuilt the form and Scripts.html behavior around Category and Task selectors.
progression.result: Description and priority autofilled while remaining editable.

progression.title: Deployment and realistic testing
progression.description: Deployed the release and tested real task creation on desktop and mobile.
progression.result: Task creation succeeded on both platforms.

problemsEncountered.problem: The prior task form relied on free-text category entry and had no guided task selector.
problemsEncountered.effect: Task creation required more typing and provided less consistency.
problemsEncountered.resolution: Replaced it with required Category and Task dropdowns backed by template data.

turningPoints.title: Layer-by-layer verification
turningPoints.description: The work deliberately tested each layer before changing the next one.
turningPoints.effectOnDirection: Deployment became the final verification stage rather than the primary debugging method.

keyDecisions.decision: Keep description and priority editable after template selection.
keyDecisions.reason: Templates should accelerate work without preventing task-specific adjustments.
consequences: Users gain speed and consistency while retaining operational flexibility.

keyDecisions.decision: Do not store Template ID yet.
keyDecisions.reason: Phase 2 focused on the user workflow and category persistence; deeper template linkage remained future work.
consequences: The task stores category and generated values, but not a durable template relationship.

narrative.methodEstablished: Create data → write service → test service → validate schema → test validation → extend startup response → test startup response → update HTML → test rendered structure → update browser behavior → test integration → deploy → test desktop → test mobile.
narrative.result: Work Queue 2.0 became a stable template-assisted operational application with a verified guided task-creation workflow.
lessonsLearned: Proving each layer before changing the next sharply reduces uncertainty.
Backend and rendered-structure tests should precede deployment.
Templates can standardize work without eliminating editable fields.
narrative.directionChange: The project moved from free-text task creation toward structured, template-assisted task creation and a more disciplined development method.
narrative.narrativeSummary: Phase 2 connected task templates from spreadsheet through service, validation, startup data, interface, browser logic, deployment, and realistic desktop/mobile use.

sections.title: Connected Task_Templates to the application
sections.contentSummary: Phase 2 began by turning the populated Task_Templates sheet into a dependable application service. New backend file TemplateService.gs Responsible for retrieving, normalizing, filtering, and sorting template records. Capabilities added Retrieve all active templates Retrieve one template by ID Return distinct categories Normalize active values and priorities Sort by order, category, and name

projectRelevance.primaryProjectContribution: Documents Phase 2 contribution: Connected Task_Templates to the application.

sections.title: Verified template retrieval before interface work
sections.contentSummary: A compact Code.gs test called TemplateService.gs → getTaskTemplates() and TemplateService.gs → getTaskTemplateCategories() . Verified totals 10 active templates 6 categories Correct IDs and names Correct descriptions and priorities Correct sorting Verified categories Carpet Care Supplies General Cleaning Windows Other General

projectRelevance.primaryProjectContribution: Documents Phase 2 contribution: Verified template retrieval before interface work.

sections.title: Expanded formal system validation
sections.contentSummary: Validation.gs now treats the template system as a required part of the Work Queue configuration. New validation coverage CONFIG.SHEETS.TASK_TEMPLATES must exist The Task_Templates sheet must exist All seven required headers must be present Complete result The final validation confirmed the configuration object, Work Queue data spreadsheet, all operational tabs, the shared location source, and all 163 active Work Queue locations.

sections.title: Rebuilt the New Task form
sections.contentSummary: The former free-text Category field was replaced with a guided, two-step template selection process. Category is now a required dropdown. Task is a new required dropdown. Task remains disabled until a category is selected. Description and Priority receive defaults but remain editable. Assigned To and Initial Note remain available.

email.subject: Work Queue 2.0 Phase 2 Update
email.body: Work Queue 2.0 now uses reusable task templates to make task creation faster and more consistent. The upgraded workflow was tested through the backend, validation, interface, desktop, and mobile, and is ready for operational use. The next recommended step is a protected template-administration screen.
